title: How to Start a Real Estate Investing Business: A Step-by-Step Guide
excerpt: Starting a real estate investing business doesn't have to be overwhelming. This step-by-step guide walks you through everything from choosing your strategy to closing your first deal.
author: AIWholesail Team
tags: how to start a real estate investing business
metaDescription: Learn how to start a real estate investing business with this step-by-step guide. Choose your strategy, build your team, and close your first deal.
metaKeywords: how to start a real estate investing business, real estate investing for beginners, wholesaling real estate, real estate business setup, real estate investing strategies

sections.content: Starting a real estate investing business is one of the most powerful financial moves you can make. But for most beginners, the hardest part isn't finding a deal — it's knowing where to begin. Do you flip houses? Wholesale contracts? Buy rentals? The options feel endless, and without a clear roadmap, it's easy to stay stuck. This guide breaks it down into clear, actionable steps so you can go from curious to closing deals faster than you think. And if you're already investing and thinking about growing, check out our [Scaling a Real Estate Investing Business: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/scaling-real-estate-investing-business) for what comes next.
Step 1: Choose Your Investing Strategy

Before you spend a single dollar or make a single call, you need to pick a strategy. Each approach has different capital requirements, risk levels, and time commitments. Trying to do everything at once is the number one mistake new investors make.

items: Wholesaling: You find undervalued properties, get them under contract, and sell the contract to another investor for an assignment fee — typically $5,000 to $20,000 per deal. This requires little to no capital and is ideal for beginners.
Fix and Flip: You buy distressed properties, renovate them, and sell for a profit. Expect to need $30,000–$100,000+ in capital or financing, plus renovation management skills.
Buy and Hold (Rentals): You purchase properties and rent them out for monthly cash flow. This builds long-term wealth but requires property management and more upfront capital.
BRRRR Method: Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat. A hybrid strategy that combines flipping and rental investing to recycle your capital.
Short-Term Rentals: You purchase properties to list on Airbnb or VRBO. High income potential, but also higher management demands and local regulation risk.

sections.content: If you're brand new and short on capital, wholesaling is the fastest path to your first paycheck in real estate. It teaches you how to find deals, negotiate, and understand property values — skills that transfer to every other strategy. Read our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to get started.
Step 2: Set Up Your Business Properly

Real estate investing is a business, and you need to treat it like one from day one. That means setting up a legal entity, opening a separate bank account, and getting your systems in place before you start making offers.
Form an LLC

Most investors operate as a Limited Liability Company (LLC). An LLC separates your personal assets from your business, which protects you if a deal goes sideways or a tenant sues you. Filing an LLC typically costs $50–$500 depending on your state. Many investors form one LLC per property or strategy — for example, one LLC for wholesaling and a separate one for rentals.
Open a Business Bank Account

Keep your business money completely separate from your personal finances. This makes bookkeeping easier, protects your LLC status, and makes tax time much simpler. Set up a business checking account and a savings account — the savings account is where you park money for taxes (set aside 25–30% of every assignment fee or profit).
Step 3: Pick Your Market

You don't have to invest where you live, but you do need to deeply understand your chosen market. Look for cities with strong population growth, job diversity, affordable entry prices, and motivated sellers. Some of the most active wholesale and flip markets right now include [Atlanta, GA](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga), [Dallas, TX](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/dallas-tx), and [Phoenix, AZ](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az) — all cities with consistent deal flow, investor demand, and strong buyer pools.
'Real estate is local. You can have a national strategy, but you need neighborhood-level knowledge to win.' — Common wisdom among top wholesalers and investors

Study your target market's average days on market, median home prices, rental rates, and vacancy rates. Free tools like Zillow, Rentometer, and your local MLS can give you a solid foundation. Once you pick a market, stay focused there for at least 6–12 months before expanding.
Step 4: Learn How to Analyze Deals

You can find a hundred leads, but if you can't quickly determine whether a deal makes financial sense, none of them will matter. The two most important numbers you need to calculate are the After Repair Value (ARV) and your Maximum Allowable Offer (MAO).
The 70% Rule for Flippers

A simple starting formula: MAO = (ARV x 70%) – Repair Costs. If a home's ARV is $250,000 and it needs $40,000 in repairs, your maximum offer is ($250,000 x 0.70) – $40,000 = $135,000. As a wholesaler, you'd subtract your assignment fee on top of that. Use our free [Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to run these numbers in seconds without doing the math by hand.
Step 5: Build Your Lead Generation System

Deals don't come to you — you have to go find them. Most successful investors use multiple lead generation channels at once. In the beginning, pick one or two channels and get really good at them before adding more.

items: Driving for Dollars: Drive neighborhoods looking for vacant, distressed, or neglected properties and contact the owners directly.
Direct Mail: Send postcards or letters to lists of motivated sellers — pre-foreclosures, probate, tax-delinquent properties, and absentee owners are common lists.
Cold Calling: Purchase lists of distressed property owners and call them. Conversion rates are low, but the cost is minimal.
Online Ads (PPC/Facebook): Run paid ads targeting motivated sellers in your market. Higher cost but faster results.
Networking: Join your local Real Estate Investors Association (REIA), attend meetups, and connect with other wholesalers, agents, and attorneys who can send you off-market deals.
Probate and Foreclosure Lists: These are publicly available in most counties and are a goldmine of motivated sellers.

sections.content: Step 6: Build Your Team

You cannot do this business alone — at least not for long. Even as a one-person operation, you'll need a network of professionals around you. Start with the essentials and grow from there. A good real estate attorney, a title company familiar with investor transactions, a reliable contractor, and a motivated seller agent are the core of most investing operations. As your business grows, you'll want to think about [how to build a real estate investing team](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/real-estate-investing-team-structure) to handle deal flow at scale.

Many investors also hire a [virtual assistant for real estate investing tasks](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/virtual-assistant-real-estate-investing) like pulling lists, skip tracing, sending mail, and managing a CRM. A good VA can cost $5–$15 per hour and free up your time to focus on closing deals rather than admin work.
Step 7: Create Systems and Processes

The investors who scale past their first few deals are the ones who document everything. That means creating Standard Operating Procedures — SOPs — for how you handle leads, make offers, manage contracts, and close transactions. Without written processes, your business depends entirely on you being in the room. With them, you can train others and eventually step back from the day-to-day. Start with just one or two core SOPs and build from there. Our guide on [building SOPs for your real estate business](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/sops-real-estate-business) walks you through exactly how to do this, even if you've never written an SOP before.

Set a goal to close your first deal within 90 days of starting. It won't be your most profitable deal, but the experience, confidence, and lessons from that first closing are worth more than any amount of theory. Speed matters early on — take imperfect action over perfect inaction every time.
How Much Money Do You Need to Start?

It depends entirely on your strategy. Wholesaling can technically be started with under $1,000 if you use free tools and hustle-based lead gen like driving for dollars and cold calling. Fix and flips require significantly more — typically $20,000–$50,000 minimum in cash or access to hard money lending. Rentals vary by market but usually require a 20–25% down payment on an investment property. The key point: you don't need to be rich to start. You need to be resourceful. For a deeper dive into getting started with minimal capital, read our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners).
